The most expensive surprises in commercial fit-out come from above the ceiling. Document what's there before design is committed.

What's Above the Ceiling — And Why It's Almost Never Documented

HVAC ductwork from previous tenancies. Pipework that doesn't match any drawing. Drainage stacks that block the intended partition layout. Above the suspended ceiling is where the previous fit-out left its mark — and where the next one discovers the surprises.

Most pre-construction documentation stops at floor level. The ceiling comes down, and the design assumptions collapse with it. Above-ceiling MEP documentation captures what's actually there before you specify the new layout.

How We Document Above-Ceiling Conditions

Thermal Imaging

FLIR first pass to identify hot and cold runs, concealed services, and thermal anomalies before any physical access.

360° Pole-Mounted Capture

Panoramic capture above the ceiling through access panels. No scaffolding, no disruption. Full visual record of ductwork, pipework, and cable runs.

Borescope and Endoscope Inspection

Reach into voids and tight spaces where the pole camera cannot go. Document what's hidden behind bulkheads and above soffits.

Narrated Conditions Commentary

Spoken walkthrough of findings. What matters for design, what matters for cost, what the M&E team needs to know.

The Cost of Not Knowing What's Up There

Before vs after: the ceiling comes down, the duct runs where the partition was supposed to go, the drainage stack blocks the kitchen layout. A single surprise can cost £5,000–£25,000 in rework, delay, and change orders.

Before documentation

Design assumes conditions. Contractor discovers conflicts on site. Change order. Programme slip. Client frustration.

After documentation

Design informed by what's actually there. M&E team knows the constraints. Fewer surprises, fewer change orders, programme stays on track.

Who Benefits From Above-Ceiling MEP Documentation

Commercial fit-out PMs

Reduce risk before tender. Inform design decisions. Avoid above-ceiling surprises.

Architects and M&E

Design with visibility. Know where services run before you specify partitions and ceilings.

Restaurant and food service

Kitchen extract, grease ducting, and drainage runs. Document before you commit to layout.

Healthcare and education

Clinical and lab services. Specialist MEP requirements. Document existing before specifying new.

Landlords and asset managers

Pre-letting documentation. Dilapidation records. Know what's above the ceiling for tenant handover.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do you need to open up the ceiling to survey above it? +

Usually no, work through existing access.

Can you identify specific services — ductwork sizes, pipe diameters, cable types? +

Document what's visible, may need M&E specialist for formal schedules.

Is above-ceiling documentation included in a standard pre-construction survey? +

Yes as standard.

What if there's no suspended ceiling — just an exposed concrete soffit? +

Document exposed services from below.
